title: Songhai Empire (c. 1375-1591)
key_facts: Largest and most powerful empire in West African history
Controlled trans-Saharan trade routes connecting North and West Africa
Major cities: Timbuktu, Gao, Djenné as centers of Islamic scholarship
Defeated by Moroccan invasion at Battle of Tondibi (1591)
causes: Strategic location on Niger River enabled agricultural surplus
Control of gold and salt trade created immense wealth
Military organization with cavalry and professional soldiers
outcome: Empire fragmented after Moroccan invasion with firearms
Trade routes disrupted leading to economic decline
Islamic learning centers declined but scholarship preserved
European powers later colonized the region

figures.name: Sunni Ali
figures.role: Founder who moved capital to Gao

figures.name: Askia Muhammad
figures.role: Greatest ruler; expanded to empire's peak

impacts: Established West Africa as center of Islamic scholarship and learning
Facilitated spread of Islam across West Africa
Created urban centers that preserved classical knowledge
Demonstrated African capacity for large-scale political organization
